title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
source: canonical Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: The input is an array of distinct integers that was sorted ascending and then rotated: some leading slice moved to the end, as in [6, 7, 8, 2, 4, 5]. Return the smallest value in the array.
constraints: every value in nums is distinct
nums was sorted ascending before the rotation

examples.explanation: The sorted order 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 was rotated so 6 leads; the minimum is 2.
The drop from 15 to 4 is the rotation point, and 4 is the minimum.

hints: The minimum is the only value smaller than the value before it, counting the array as circular.
Compare the middle value with the value at the right end: that pair tells you which side holds the drop.
While lo < hi: if nums[mid] > nums[hi] the minimum is right of mid, so lo = mid + 1; otherwise it is at mid or left, so hi = mid. Return nums[lo].
solution: Binary search on the rotation point: when nums[mid] exceeds nums[hi] the minimum lies strictly right of mid; otherwise it lies at mid or left. The range shrinks to one element: O(log n) time, O(1) space.
failureHint: hidden tests include no rotation, a single value, and the minimum at either end

visible.failNote: find where the sorted order restarts
the minimum can sit at the very end
